title: Bar Hei Hei
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned at the end of Avot, chapter 5, where he said: “According to the pain is the reward.” The Tosafot Yom Tov there cites in the name of the Rashbam, cited in Midrash Shmuel, that Ben Bag Bag and Ben Hei Hei were converts, and in order to hide them from informers they changed their names; so too Tosafot wrote on Chagigah 9b. There [it is related] that Bar Hei Hei asked Hillel: “What is the meaning of what is written, ‘Then you shall again distinguish between the one who serves God,’” etc. Hyman asks: if he lived in Hillel’s days, of whom were they afraid if they were converts, since then, in Temple times, the government was in Israel’s hands? He considers it more likely that there were two: one in the time of the Tannaim after the destruction, in the time of the persecutions, who is called Ben Hei Hei; but the Ben Hei Hei who asked Hillel — this is not Hillel the Tanna but Hillel, Rabbi’s grandson, brother of Rabbi Yehudah Nesia. This Bar Hei Hei is the one whom Eliyahu is said to have asked, “What is the meaning of what is written, ‘Behold, I have refined you,’” etc. Hyman likewise infers from the passage that he was an Amora, since they said there: “Eliyahu said to Bar Hei Hei — and some say to Rabbi Elazar,” etc.

notes.text: The source’s HaHa/HiHi spellings remain recorded and Hyman’s two-person/later-Hillel reconstruction remains his conjecture. Bar Hei Hei, rather than Hillel, is the subject of the clause about Eliyahu’s question. The political premise is Hyman’s argument, not a new historical endorsement.

The inspected Chagigah 9b directly has Bar Hei Hei questioning Hillel and Eliyahu addressing Bar Hei Hei, with an alternative Elazar attribution. Hyman’s proposed two people, later Hillel, conversion-name explanation and political argument remain attributed; the exact Rashbam, Midrash Shmuel and Tosafot Yom Tov editions were not inspected.
